notes: §1985:XII.2.3 SR10: 'If the word COPY appears in a comment-entry or in the place where a comment-entry may appear, it is considered part of the comment-entry.' The fixed-form logical conversion (FixedFormConverter#CommentEntryOf, from ConvertLine) recognises an AUTHOR/INSTALLATION/DATE-WRITTEN/DATE-COMPILED/SECURITY header in the identification division (DivisionCursor) and discards its entry up to the next Area-A word (§1985:IV.7.3.3) before the COPY driver runs, carrying an undecided candidate to CommentEntryResolver#Resolve, so no COPY in the entry is ever a statement; from 2002 the paragraphs are refused COBOL0902. Probes at 85: COPY of a missing text after AUTHOR. on its line, on the next Area-B line, split across two Area-B lines, with REPLACING, and after an unclosed quotation mark all ignored (OK / REAL COPY printed, rc 0); a library text whose AUTHOR/INSTALLATION entries hold COPY is copied with no GR12 nested-COPY refusal; COPY in Area A after AUTHOR. ME. is a real COPY. The witness is AUTHOR. COPY NOSUCHTEXT.

next.reason: 1985 makes the word COPY inside a comment-entry (AUTHOR, INSTALLATION, DATE-WRITTEN, DATE-COMPILED, SECURITY paragraphs) part of the comment-entry. 2023 has no comment-entries at all: the term and those paragraphs do not occur anywhere in ISO 1989:2023, and §2023:7.2.3.3 SR1 places COPY only where a character-string or separator may appear in source or library text. No 2023 rule carries this requirement.
